# Miso Music Protocol

> Developer documentation for the Miso Music Protocol, a small set of Sui Move primitives for identifying musical compositions, recordings, and releases and connecting them to optional rights, metadata, and payment packages.

The core Move package is `miso_music`. A `Composition` is the written work, a `Recording` is a particular master with an immutable composition ID, and a `Release` is an ordered list of recording IDs. Each composition and recording has its own fixed-supply share type. Admin capabilities control extension writes and the licenses a work grants; owning shares alone does not grant those powers. Anyone can create a release of shared recordings; the Framework's release license records each recording admin's authorization and the release's revenue splits. The pages describe the core sources recorded as published on Sui mainnet (`miso_music` at bc547c79, `miso_party` at b16e0598).

Read the music overview first, then the separate Party protocol, Composition, Recording, and Release. Share types are explained within the overview and the composition/recording pages. The Move Packages sidebar groups Party Protocol, Music Protocol, and Framework. Party Protocol contains its overview and an Extensions group with one page per extension. Music Protocol covers Composition, Recording, and Release, followed by an Extensions group whose package pages are grouped by object. Framework groups its package pages as Economics, Records and Player, and Actions and Libraries. Every package in misofm/framework has its own page, titled with the package name. These pages explain the protocol design with inline excerpts from the actual Move contracts; use the supplemental Move source guide only when inspecting the implementation. Add only the extensions needed for the product. A core object link is not proof of real-world authorship or a license, and holding shares pays nothing by itself: payment depends on a funded royalty pool and registered stakes. Pin compatible source revisions and verify published package IDs before constructing transactions against a network.

## Start Here

- [Overview](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/index.md): The song/master/release model, industry identifier lookups and access, Music's Shared Ledger, share types and fixed supply, the limits of canonical state, and Miso Link's SuiNS bridge.

## Party Protocol

- [Party](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/index.md): The identity-only `miso_party` generation published on mainnet: a Party is only an ID, its one derived admin cap is checked by `uid_mut`, and names, profiles, genres, and group membership are extensions. Covers attribution, unverified identity claims, the creation event and error, the mainnet package ID, and what changed from earlier generations.
- [Party Protocol Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/extensions/index.md): Overview of how Party extensions attach through uid_mut with permissionless reads and full-value events; the four extensions (name, profile, genre, group), group membership in brief, administrator claims versus proof, the open genre vocabulary, and compatibility. Each extension has its own page below.
- [Party Name](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/extensions/party-name/index.md): A display name under PartyNameKey, kept separate from the profile; set_name with its empty check before the cap and no on-chain maximum; setting the name in the creating transaction; clearing and views; names are unverified claims; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Party Profile](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/extensions/party-profile/index.md): The Profile struct and its limits (bio_short 1-300 bytes, bio_long 1-8,192 bytes, ISO country code, up to 10 unique ISO 639-1 languages); the card is always replaced whole; validation before the cap; equal cards are silent; what is not stored here; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Party Genre](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/extensions/party-genre/index.md): Genre tags on a Party, one PartyGenreKey(ID) field per genre; listing over RPC; no ranking; add_genre takes a Genre from the permissionless vocabulary; removal by ID; genre IDs shared with release and recording genres; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Party Group](https://docs.miso.fm/move/party-protocol/extensions/party-group/index.md): Two-halves membership (PartyMemberKey on the group, PartyGroupMembershipKey on the member) and its state table; add_member and the PartyGroupInvite object; join in a later transaction, decline, leave, and removal; finding members, groups, and invites over RPC; nonrecursive membership that grants no rights; failure cases, events, and deployment.

## Music Protocol

- [Composition](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/composition/index.md): Why the written work has an identity independent of recordings, its unique share type, fixed supply, allocation and royalty participation, its minimal Move definition, capability-gated extension access, and optional extensions.
- [Recording](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/recording/index.md): Why a master has independent identity and shares, its share-type constants, fixed supply and royalty participation, an immutable composition relationship, its Move object and creation event definitions, its one derived admin cap, and release authorization recorded on the recording by the Framework's release license.
- [Release](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/release/index.md): Ordered track lists of 1-255 distinct recordings with fresh release IDs, ReleaseTrack proofs that let anyone release shared recordings, the opening checks of `release::new`, why recording admins' authorization lives in a release license, release administration, failure cases, events, and the earlier consent-and-salt generation.


## Packages, Protocol Extensions, and Framework

- [Packages Overview](https://docs.miso.fm/move/index.md): How core identities, data-model extensions, and business-logic framework packages fit together; core share validation, identifier resolution, compatibility, and licensing.
- [Music Protocol Extensions](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/index.md): Overview of how music extensions attach to the core, and the inventory of composition, recording, and release extensions by object, with compatibility and licensing. Each extension has its own page below.
- [Composition Title](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/composition-title/index.md): A composition's preferred title under CompositionTitleKey; non-empty and at most 300 bytes, checked before the cap; type-bound cap authorization; silent equal sets and absent clears; title as presentation rather than identity or rights; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Composition Credits](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/composition-credits/index.md): A VecMap of Credit values keyed by Party ID (at most 50, in insertion order); the six writing roles and the absence of a publisher role; building a credit and adding it in one transaction; the credited Party is not asked; changing a credit by removing and re-adding it; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Composition Lyrics](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/composition-lyrics/index.md): Zstd-compressed lyrics keyed by ISO 639-1 language; what is checked on-chain (non-empty, at most 32,768 compressed bytes, valid code) versus not (frame, decompression, UTF-8, actual language); untrusted-decoder guidance; clearing leaves bytes in event history; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Recording Version](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-version/index.md): A version name such as Live or Radio Edit under RecordingVersionKey; non-empty and at most 300 bytes, checked before the cap; only a change emits; building a display title from the composition title plus the version; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Recording Credits](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-credits/index.md): A VecMap of credits (at most 150, 10 roles each) keyed by Party ID; the 33-role RecordingPartyRole enum and its levels; Primary and Featured roles versus levels; is_primary_artist and is_featured_artist; billing order; independence from release credits; the add_credit function; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Recording Advisory](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-advisory/index.md): The Explicit, NotExplicit, and Cleaned advisory values and why no advisory differs from NotExplicit; constructors and checks for an enum that cannot be matched outside its module; set and clear gated by the recording cap; silent repeats; reads that abort with ENoAdvisory; events and deployment.
- [Recording Genre](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-genre/index.md): Genres of the recording itself versus the release-level claim; one RecordingGenreKey(ID) field per genre with no order or primary genre; add_genre takes a Genre from the vocabulary, which can be created in the same transaction; removal by ID; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Recording Language](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-language/index.md): Three states: no field means no claim, an empty list means instrumental, and a list gives the languages with the first predominant; validated ISO 639-1 codes; at most 10 with no repeats, order kept and reordering counted as a change; clearing; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Recording Master](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/recording-master/index.md): Masters as references to frozen Audio objects keyed by Audio ID, several side by side; the verify_audio, add_master, freeze flow in one transaction; trusting only pinned verifier types; a master is a claim, not proof of authorship; release authorization covers every master; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Title](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-title/index.md): A release's preferred title stored verbatim; non-empty and at most 300 bytes, checked before the cap; release::EUnauthorized for a wrong cap; setting it before sharing in the creating transaction; presentation not covered by recording authorization; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Cover Art](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-cover-art/index.md): An album cover plus one override slot per track via ReleaseTrackData; CoverArt Walrus blob IDs that are not checked; how a track cover resolves (override, then album cover); set and clear functions; the cap checked before the track index; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Credits](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-credits/index.md): Top-line billing as a VecMap from Party ID to a credit with exactly one Primary or Featured role; at most 50 credits; billing names separate from party_name; no consent from the credited Party; remove and re-add to change a credit; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Description](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-description/index.md): One verbatim description per release with no normalization; non-empty and at most 8,192 bytes, checked before the cap; repeat sets are no-ops; the set event carries the full text; an unverified statement by the release admin; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Genre](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-genre/index.md): Product-level genre tags compared with recording genres; one ReleaseGenreKey(ID) field per genre; listing over RPC; no order or primary genre; a permissionless, uncurated vocabulary; offline derive_address; removal by ID; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Release Kind](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/extensions/release-kind/index.md): A free-form kind label such as Album, EP, or Mixtape, not a closed vocabulary or derived from the tracks; stored verbatim, 1 to 32 bytes, checked before the cap; silent equal sets; clearing and views; failure cases, events, and deployment.
- [Framework](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/index.md): The misofm/framework packages: how a release sale reaches recording and composition shareholders, economics (royalty pools, recording revenue shares, release licenses, royalty grants and advances), Records and their sale, the Player, Actions, libraries, renamed and retired packages, core pins, and which recorded deployments match the source. Every Framework package has its own page below.
- [Royalty Pool](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/royalty-pool/index.md): One pool per work and payout currency; stake registration before sharing, deposits, exact remainder accounting, the once-per-timestamp settle guard, claims, failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Recording Revenue Share](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/recording-revenue-share/index.md): A recording permanently gives its composition the composition's published rate of its shares, held as the composition's stake; terms and rate, the exact share count, registration and sweep into the composition pool, withdrawal, why it is not a copyright license, failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Release License](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/release-license/index.md): Per-track splits set once, recording admins' authorization written on each recording, the permanent Authorized state, forwarding release revenue to each track's pool regardless of authorization, collecting at the license's address with redeem_and_forward, failure cases, events carrying the license ID and authorized count, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Royalty Grant](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/royalty-grant/index.md): Locking a stake to pay a recipient part of its royalties in one currency until an amount is repaid or a term ends; grants start pending until the recipient activates them and the owner can cancel until then; terms and schemes, owner and recipient caps, how each sweep is split and rounded, guarded buyout and waive, reclaim, timing caveats, failure cases, events naming the payees, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Royalty Advance](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/royalty-advance/index.md): On-chain advances escrowed in an offer; accepting pays the owner, creates an active royalty grant with the provider as recipient, and returns the grant's owner cap in one transaction. Offer creation, acceptance by exact stake size, cancellation consuming the provider cap, expiry and refunds, failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Record](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/record/index.md): Pressing versus Record; the Release, Pressing, Record identity chain; sequential editions gated by the release admin cap; fixed max_supply and gap-free numbering; Distributor witness authorization and new; Records carry lineage and number but no purchase data, so access never depends on spending; witness privacy and immutability rules; failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Record Sale](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/record-sale/index.md): One fixed price in one currency per Pressing, set once by authorize and never changed; free sales and tips through release_license::forward; the purchase function and its check order; the authorized release license requirement; where money goes; stopping a sale by revoking the witness; the private Witness; failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Player](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/player/index.md): A listener's on-chain root as a slim, transferable key + store Player that anyone can create; holding Records and funds at its address; extending through uid_mut; owning, lending, and selling a Player; events and the mainnet deployment.
- [Party Wallet](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/party-wallet/index.md): The Party Action for a Party's object and accumulator-funds inboxes: receive, receive_balance, and redeem_balance gated by the core uid_mut, composing with a vault lease in one transaction, why there is no wallet plugin, never sending the PartyAdminCap to its own Party, failure cases, events, and deployments.
- [Player Wallet](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/player-wallet/index.md): The Player counterpart of party_wallet: receive objects and coins sent to a Player's address, or redeem its accumulator funds, authorized by &mut Player and returned to the caller; composition in one transaction, failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Vault](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/vault/index.md): Generic capability custody: Vault, VaultAdminCap, and VaultRegistry; derived IDs and discovery; hot-potato Borrow leases returning the exact object in the same transaction; plugin witnesses and the risk of authorizing constructible types; withdraw, restore, and destroy; failure cases, events, and deployments.
- [Enclave](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/enclave/index.md): The Apache-2.0 EnclavePolicy<App> library: one AWS Nitro enclave image per App, permissionless registration of an enclave key from its attestation document, on-chain verification of signed intent messages, PCR changes that retire every older key, the TypeScript SDK in the package's sdk directory, failure cases, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Audio](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/audio/index.md): The Audio<AudioVerifier> record over five measured facts and its derived address; one Audio per verifier and facts; the checks new makes; freezing in the same transaction as add_master; the BLAKE3 PCM digest for checking a file; pinning trusted verifier types; errors, events, and the mainnet deployment.
- [Audio Verifier](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/audio-verifier/index.md): Creating Audio from facts signed by an enclave key registered on the AudioVerifier's EnclavePolicy through the enclave package; the signed BCS intent message; the trust model (what Sui checks, what is trusted to the enclave, AWS Nitro, and the policy-cap holder); setting PCRs and registering enclaves; errors and events; the mainnet deployment, whose policy had no PCRs set when checked.
- [Credit](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/credit/index.md): The Credit<Role> value: a non-empty display name of at most 200 bytes with 1-50 distinct roles; how the composition, recording, and release credits extensions use it and their extra limits; replacing a credit by remove then add; errors and deployments.
- [Genre](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/genre/index.md): Frozen Genre objects whose IDs derive from their names in a GenreRegistry; permissionless creation and naming rules; create, tag, and freeze in one transaction; the recording, release, and party genre extensions; errors, events, and per-generation registries.
- [Cover Art](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/cover-art/index.md): The CoverArt value with Walrus blob IDs for a still image and an optional animation; new never aborts; nothing on-chain checks that a blob exists, is an image, or is unencrypted; use by release cover art for album and per-track covers; deployments.
- [Release Track Data](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/release-track-data/index.md): ReleaseTrackData<Data>, a vector checked against the release track count at construction; new, filled, borrow, and borrow_mut; access control and events left to the storing extension; the length-not-identity caveat; use by release cover art; mainnet deployment.
- [Release Track Iterator](https://docs.miso.fm/move/framework/release-track-iterator/index.md): Why typed per-track calls need a programmable-transaction loop; ReleaseTrackIterator<Witness> with new, next, and finish; in-order and visit-every-track guarantees; the consumer pattern; checking each recording ID and keeping the witness private; failure cases and mainnet deployment.

## Optional

- [Move Source Guide](https://docs.miso.fm/move/music-protocol/integrating/index.md): Supplemental implementation material: reproduce the pinned core tests, pin the dependency, the recorded mainnet package and registry IDs with their publish transaction, the new/share creation flow for each object, and differences from earlier generations.

## Source Repositories

- [Miso Music Protocol](https://github.com/misofm/music-protocol): Core Move package, templates, source modules, and Apache 2.0 license.
- [Party Protocol](https://github.com/misofm/party-protocol): Apache-2.0 identity primitive in `miso_party`, separate from the music core.
- [Miso Framework](https://github.com/misofm/framework): FSL-1.1-ALv2 monorepo (with the Apache-2.0 enclave package) of separately published Move packages: music and party extensions, royalty pools, recording revenue shares, release licenses, royalty grants and advances, Records and their sale, the Player, Actions, and libraries.
- [Miso Link](https://github.com/misofm/link): SuiNS-based mapping of legacy industry identifiers to on-chain object addresses. A mapping is an assertion by its namespace controller, not an official registry record or rights verification.
